external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and may log in to the build runner to initiate a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: The text does not place developers in a trust zone or describe their authentication.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the image registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be used by developers to initiate a rebuild of main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand; that path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release image SHA for the estate and responds to store server release queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The text does not state what a store server presents to the controller.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Till software running as a container on small servers in store back offices.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: This represents the till software running across the approximately 1,200 stores.

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: The self-hosted git server where developers push branches and from which the build runner fetches source and the dependency lockfile.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry that stores finished container images tagged with commit SHAs and serves them to store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_stores.name: dependency lockfile
data_stores.description: The dependency lockfile used during dependency resolution.
data_stores.notes: The lockfile is taken as given; the runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_stores.name: release record
data_stores.description: The record identifying which image SHA the estate should be running.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: merge main
data_flows.description: A developer merges changes to main, which starts a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and initiates a rebuild of main by hand.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source and the dependency lockfile from the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry to resolve dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: request release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The token is a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: image SHA and request to make it the current release

data_flows.name: ask current release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller which release is current.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.
data_flows.data_description: current release image SHA request and response

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of approximately 1,200 stores containing the store servers running the till software.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Build and deploy pipeline for the in-store estate.

trust_boundaries.name: retail WAN
trust_boundaries.description: The WAN carrying traffic between the stores and the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet location of the public package registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet
